summary: The board-specific logic is MAME's Gaelco driver rewritten in Verilog. The sprite engine walks sprite RAM in the same loop as draw_sprites, with the same offsets and attribute handling. Tile/sprite priority is MAME's screen_update_squash draw order and pri_mask table squeezed into a 16-step rank function, with MAME's 'colour >= 0x3c means top priority' rule copied in. The VRAM decryptor is gaelcrpt.cpp's decrypt() line for line. Nothing is organised around the board's own chips, raster counters or net names; the one real departure (detecting the second half of a 32-bit write from bus cycles instead of the PC) is needed just to make it work in hardware.

findings.signal: Tile/sprite priority encodes MAME's draw order
findings.note: The rank() table orders {category, layer, pen[3]} in exactly the sequence of the 16 tilemap draw() calls in screen_update_squash (cat 3 L1/LAYER1, L1/LAYER0, L0/LAYER1, L0/LAYER0, ..., including the swapped order for category 1). Per-pixel priority is MAME's batch draw order flattened into a rank, not a board PROM or mixer.

findings.signal: Sprite priority thresholds stand in for MAME pri_mask
findings.note: Sprite priority 0..3 maps to rank thresholds 12/10/8/4 and priority 4 to 31 (never hidden). These are MAME's pri_mask values (0xff00, |0xf0f0, |0xcccc, |0xaaaa, 0) against the screen.priority() values 0/1/2/4/8 written by screen_update_squash, turned into a compare.
prio_r is forced to 4 when the colour is >= 6'h3c. That is MAME's emulator heuristic (color >= m_sprite_palette_force_high gives priority = 4), not a decode a board would plausibly have.

findings.signal: Sprite list walk transliterates draw_sprites loop
findings.note: The FSM starts at index 2043 (0x800-4-1), reads words i, i+2 and i+3, steps i-=4 while i>=7, i.e. MAME's for (i = 0x800-4-1; i >= 3; i -= 4). It never reads word 1, which is unused in MAME's format too. Same descending order and word selection as the C loop.

findings.signal: Sprite attribute math identical to MAME
findings.note: sy = 240 - y, sx - 0x0f, size from bit 11, code &= ~3 for 16x16, flip x/y from bits 14/15, colour from w2[14:9], and cell code = number + x_offset{0,2} + y_offset{0,1} with flip handling via ex/ey. These are MAME's expressions repeated one for one.

findings.signal: VRAM decryptor is MAME's decrypt() verbatim
findings.note: Same swap/type selectors, same four bitswap tables, the same res ^= param2, k1/k2 add-in-field steps with 0xffc0/0x003f/0x07c0/0xf800 masks, and the same final bitswap. Parameters 0x0f/0x4228 are MAME's squash values. It is the C algorithm as combinational logic, not a model of the custom chip's structure.

findings.signal: Write pairing from bus cycles instead of PC
findings.note: MAME spots the second half of a 32-bit write by comparing the CPU PC. The core instead treats back-to-back AS cycles to consecutive VRAM word offsets as a pair, which is how bus-attached hardware would have to do it. It is a necessary replacement rather than a board-derived design, so it is weak evidence.

code = 0x4000 + data[15:2], flipx/flipy = data[1:0], colour = data2[5:0], category = data2[7:6]. Even the 0x4000 offset, which in MAME is a gfx-element index, is kept as an organising constant. The per-pixel fetch pipeline itself is ordinary FPGA engineering.

Range-compare chip selects one-to-one with MAME's map entries (cs_clrint for irqack_w at 0x10800c, cs_okibank for oki_bankswitch_w, cs_outlatch for the LS259 select(0x70)). No PAL or 74138-style decode. The map has to match, but the structure and naming follow the handler list.

findings.signal: Generic video timing, no board raster chain
findings.note: A parameterised VGA-style counter (320 visible plus guessed porches, VTOTAL 272) with the IRQ at the end of the visible area. There are no board H/V counter bits driving fetch phases, and per-layer scroll fudge constants (+3, -1, +16) sit in squash_video.v:23-26. Neither board- nor MAME-derived.
Fixed 0x00000-0x2ffff and banked 0x30000-0x3ffff with a 4-bit bank. This is required behaviour; the shape is MAME's address-map description, but any correct core must share it.
